definitions.explanation: A personality trait of being reluctant to step forward or assert oneself. Describes someone who holds back in social situations.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{引|ひ}っ{込|こ}み{思案|じあん}な{性格|せいかく}だ。
{引|ひ}っ{込|こ}み{思案|じあん}だった{娘|むすめ}が、{最近|さいきん}{積極的|せっきょくてき}になってきた。
examples.english: My daughter, who used to be withdrawn, has recently become more outgoing.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{込|こ}み{思案|じあん}では{商売|しょうばい}はうまくいかない。
examples.english: You can't succeed in business if you're too timid.

notes: Literally 'pulling-back thinking' — the idea of hesitating and overthinking before acting. Often used with な to modify nouns: {引|ひ}っ{込|こ}み{思案|じあん}な{人|ひと}. Describes a mild, everyday form of shyness rather than clinical anxiety. Similar to {内気|うちき} (introverted) but emphasizes the tendency to hold back rather than a quiet nature.
